summary: This code extracts metadata from all MDX blog posts in a `/blog` directory using Webpack's dynamic loading. It parses frontmatter (the YAML header) from each post, normalizes file paths and image references, and returns a filtered array of post metadata objects. By default it excludes draft and unlisted posts, but callers can opt back in via flags.

explanations.99: The `require.context` call tells Webpack to dynamically load all MDX/Markdown files from the blog directory. The `!!` prefix at the start of the path is crucial—it forces Webpack to use a custom loader (frontmatter-loader) instead of the default blog plugin, so draft posts don't crash the production build.
explanations.110: `.keys()` returns an array of all file paths that Webpack found matching our pattern; we then `.map()` over them to extract metadata from each one.
explanations.112: We call `posts(key)` to load the actual file content for this path. TypeScript treats it as an object with a `frontMatter` property containing the parsed YAML.
explanations.116: If a Markdown file under `blog/` has no title, we skip it—it's probably a fragment or helper file, not a published article, so we return `null` to filter it out later.
explanations.120: We extract the directory path from the file path: if the file is `./my-post/index.mdx`, `dir` becomes `my-post`. This directory name becomes part of the post's URL.
explanations.123: If the author explicitly set a `slug` in frontmatter, we use that as the post's URL path; otherwise we build the path from the folder structure (line 128).
explanations.132: If the image path starts with `./`, it's a relative reference to a local file in the post's folder, so we convert it to an absolute web path like `/blog/my-post/image.png`.
explanations.151: The `filter` with the type guard `post is BlogPostMetadata` removes all the `null` entries we returned for non-article files, and TypeScript now knows remaining items are valid `BlogPostMetadata` objects.
explanations.153: This second filter respects the caller's preferences: if `includeDrafts` is false, we exclude posts where `draft` is true; same logic applies to `includeUnlisted`.
